title: Inheritance Builder with Multiple Mixins & Super Dispatch
problemStatement: Implement `createSubclass(Parent, ChildConstructor, methods, mixins)` that sets up full prototypal inheritance without ES6 classes, wires `Child.prototype.__proto__` to `Parent.prototype`, copies mixin methods safely, and attaches `_super` to invoke parent methods.
interviewTrap: Assigning `Child.prototype = Parent.prototype` shares the exact same prototype object, causing methods added to Child to pollute Parent.

testCases.name: Correctly wires prototype chain
testCases.testFn: function Animal(name) { this.name = name; } function Dog(name) { Animal.call(this, name); } createSubclass(Animal, Dog); const d = new Dog('Rex'); return d instanceof Animal;

testCases.name: Executes super method via _super
testCases.testFn: function Animal(name) { this.name = name; } Animal.prototype.speak = function() { return 'ANIMAL: ' + this.name; }; function Dog(name) { Animal.call(this, name); } createSubclass(Animal, Dog, { speak() { return this._super('speak'); } }); const d = new Dog('Rex'); return d.speak();

testCases.name: Integrates mixins into prototype
testCases.testFn: function Animal() {} function Dog() {} const wagMixin = { wag() { return 'wagging'; } }; createSubclass(Animal, Dog, {}, [wagMixin]); const d = new Dog(); return d.wag();

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Every JS object has an internal `[[Prototype]]` link. Property lookup walks this chain until the property is found or `null` is reached (`Object.prototype.__proto__ === null`). Modifying a property on an instance creates an 'own property' shadowing the prototype's property.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Prototypal Inheritance & Clean Method Composition.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Prototypal Inheritance & Clean Method Composition is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Assigning `Child.prototype = Parent.prototype` shares the exact same prototype object, causing methods added to Child to pollute Parent.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.
